name: Liquid Morph
use: Openers, brand stings, and turning one object into another.
how: Liquid blobs merge into the shape of the showcase case, the real case lands, then it melts back.
avoid: the piece needs hard, technical or data-driven energy; the goo reads as playful

name: Fly-Through
use: Going from a big claim to the proof in one cut.
how: The headline speeds through the lens while the destination scene is already waiting underneath.
src: Contra, Wonder, Bolt launch films via motion-video-kit
avoid: the headline is long or needs to be read slowly, or the scene underneath has nothing worth revealing

name: Kinetic Type
use: Hooks in the first 3 seconds and music-cut social edits.
how: Huge words swap in place on the beat with pops, mask reveals and colour slams.
avoid: the message needs more than ~2 words per beat, or the tone is calm or luxury

name: Showcase Hero
use: Making one object feel physical and premium.
how: A 3D turn on a measured curve, with glare and edge light that show the angle.
avoid: you need to show several items or explain steps; it is a single-object hero

name: Exploded Layers
use: Product anatomy: showing what something is made of.
how: Case, label, card and inner frame separate with labelled callouts, then close up again.
avoid: the object has no meaningful layers, or labels would need more than a few words

name: Stack and Fan
use: Collection reveals and showing variety.
how: Cards stack up, fan out as the camera pulls back, then collapse to one.
avoid: you only have one item, or the items need to be read in detail

name: Artifact Ring
use: One line of copy surrounded by the things it's about.
how: Passes, cases and chips orbit a tilted ring while the sentence builds word by word.
avoid: the copy is longer than ~4 short words, or you need the objects themselves to be read

name: Materializing Result
use: Reveal a result or summary screen step by step without a real UI.
how: Dots gather into a card, then the header and 3 rows wipe in with spring checkmarks; reverses by scattering.
avoid: the message is a single word or number; the dot gather needs a layout worth materializing

name: Persistent Rails
use: Explain two inputs flowing into one destination.
how: Fixed glowing rails carry drops from two source chips into a liquid-filled hub while the headline swaps over 3 beats.
avoid: you have more than two sources or need numbers on screen; the layout is built for exactly two lanes

name: Logo Portal
use: Logo open or close; a brand mark that opens into the product world.
how: Seamless Droste zoom through a pass's punched hole into a hub scene, then into the mini pass inside it.
avoid: the viewer must read body copy; text is only readable during the short holds

name: Perspective Fold
use: 3-step how-it-works sequences.
how: Panels hinge back into a glowing floor strip and the next panel rises out of it, with a progress rail below.
avoid: steps need more than a headline and one short line, or you have more than 3-4 steps in 6 s

name: Step Carousel
use: Ordered lists of 3-7 short words (steps, features).
how: Tilted 3D word drum snaps item by item; the active word glows and the background hue follows it.
avoid: labels are long phrases; the drum only reads with single short words

name: Camera Journey
use: A whole flow in one continuous shot; roadmaps and overviews.
how: One camera glides across 4 stations on a lit rail, with zoom dips between holds.
avoid: each step needs a long read; holds are only 0.8 s

name: Recursive Zoom
use: Hypnotic endless sting behind a fixed caption.
how: A case holds a room whose pedestal holds the same case; constant exponential push, seamless.
avoid: the scene needs to change or tell steps; it is one idea on repeat

name: Velvet Standard
use: Calm luxury spotlights and expensive end cards.
how: A showcase case sways in a hairline frame while wide-tracked captions cross.
src: HyperFrames Velvet Standard · LottieFiles premium timing
avoid: you need energy, fast information, or more than two short captions

name: Colour-Field Lockup
use: End-card lockups with a wordmark and URL.
how: A wordmark assembles from split halves over an orbiting colour field, then the field swallows it.
avoid: the wordmark is long (more than ~5 wide letters) or the scene must stay text-dense

name: Swiss Grid
use: Hard-cut rhythm, counts and "same every time" proof beats.
how: A 4x3 Swiss grid lights one cell per beat while a giant numeral counts.
avoid: you need soft, emotional motion or real data (the numeral is a beat counter, not a statistic)

name: Tile Wipe
use: Chapter breaks in step-by-step explainers.
how: A diagonal cascade of foil and colour tiles flips one chapter card to the next.
avoid: the mood is quiet or the cut needs to be invisible

name: Liquid Chrome
use: Abstract hero openers behind a headline.
how: A chrome liquid surface where a mark rises as an iridescent tube, then sinks back (WebGL2).
avoid: you need to show a real product or UI, or render time is tight (WebGL, ~seconds per frame)

name: Silk Ribbons
use: Slow, elegant backdrops for a product.
how: Folding silk ribbons of light drift behind a levitating showcase case (WebGL2).
avoid: the message is urgent or the scene must render fast (two WebGL passes)

name: Aura Bloom
use: Heartbeat or "it's live" pulse moments.
how: Aura rings bloom off a pass on a lub-dub beat over a mesh gradient (WebGL2).
avoid: the scene needs stillness or must render quickly (WebGL)

name: Reeded Glass
use: Premium product reveals and glass-wipe transitions.
how: Fluted glass slides across a hero shot and reveals it sharp, with RGB dispersion (WebGL2).
avoid: the copy must be readable from the first frame (it starts behind the glass), or on low-power playback where WebGL is unavailable

name: Halftone Glyphs
use: Data and "how it works" beats; print-meets-tech textures.
how: An object prints itself out of a living halftone and glyph field, then dissolves back (WebGL2).
avoid: the object has fine detail that must stay legible (a 10 px cell grid eats small type), or the brand is soft and organic

name: Flow Field
use: Calm generative openers that resolve into a mark.
how: Thousands of drifting particle streaks gather into a glowing mark, hold, and release.
avoid: you need a crisp product shot or the message needs reading in the first second

name: Type Ring
use: Editorial titles and end cards.
how: Rings of display and mono type counter-rotate around a hero object.
avoid: the ring copy is long (it must fit the circumference) or the format is very wide and short

name: Squash and Stretch
use: Playful "you're in" or "approved" beats.
how: A pass drops, squashes, bounces and gets stamped, then jumps away.
avoid: the tone is serious or luxury, or the object must not be distorted (product photos, logos with strict usage rules)

name: Pixel Resolve
use: Game-y hooks and loading-to-reveal moments.
how: Shuffling pixels snap into a mosaic of the hero, a scan line resolves it crisp, then it de-rezzes.
avoid: the brand is elegant or quiet, or the piece is long-form (the shuffle is busy)

name: Foil Confetti
use: Success and launch celebrations.
how: A stamp slams onto a hero object and foil confetti bursts, flutters and gathers back.
avoid: the message is serious or the screen must stay calm for reading (confetti crosses the text)
